plan: 2 Samuel 5:1-3; 1 Chronicles 11:1-3; 1 Chronicles 12:23-40; 2 Samuel 5:17-25; 1 Chronicles 14:8-17; 2 Samuel 5:6-10; 1 Chronicles 11:4-9; 1 Chronicles 3:4b; 2 Samuel 5:13, 4-5, 11-12; 1 Chronicles 14:1-2; 1 Chronicles 13:1-5; 2 Samuel 6:1-11; 1 Chronicles 13:6-14

readings.title: David Anointed King at Hebron
readings.text:
[2 Samuel 5:1] And all the tribes of Yisra’ěl came to Daviḏ at Ḥeḇron and spoke, saying, “Look, we are your bone and your flesh.
[2] “Formerly, when Sha’ul was sovereign over us, you were the one who led Yisra’ěl out and brought them in. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to you, <dq>‘Shepherd <dn>את</dn> My people Yisra’ěl, and be ruler over Yisra’ěl.’</dq> ”
[3] And all the elders of Yisra’ěl came to the sovereign at Ḥeḇron, and Sovereign Daviḏ made a covenant with them at Ḥeḇron before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And they anointed <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ sovereign over Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: All Israel Gathers to David
readings.text:
[1 Chronicles 11:1] And all Yisra’ěl came together to Daviḏ at Ḥeḇron, saying, “See, we are your bone and your flesh.
[2] “Also, in time past, even when Sha’ul was sovereign, you were the one who led Yisra’ěl out and brought them in. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> said to you, <dq>‘Shepherd <dn>את</dn> My people Yisra’ěl, and be ruler over My people Yisra’ěl.’</dq> ”
[3] So all the elders of Yisra’ěl came to the sovereign at Ḥeḇron, and Daviḏ made a covenant with them at Ḥeḇron before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And they anointed <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ sovereign over Yisra’ěl, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> by Shemu’ěl.

readings.title: The Armies That Came to Hebron
The Philistines Defeated
readings.text:
[2 Samuel 5:17] And the Philistines heard that they had anointed <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ sovereign over Yisra’ěl, and all the Philistines went up to search for <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ, but Daviḏ heard and went down to the stronghold.
[18] And the Philistines came and spread themselves out in the Valley of Repha’im.
[19] And Daviḏ inquired of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “Do I go up against the Philistines? Do You give them into my hand?” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Daviḏ, <dq>“Go up, for I shall certainly give <dn>את</dn> the Philistines into your hand.”</dq>
[20] And Daviḏ came to Ba‛al Peratsim, and Daviḏ struck them there. And he said, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has broken through <dn>את</dn> my enemies before me, like a breakthrough of water.” So he called the name of that place Ba‛al Peratsim.
[21] And they left <dn>את</dn> their images there, and Daviḏ and his men took them away.
[22] And the Philistines again came up and were spread out in the Valley of Repha’im.
[23] And when Daviḏ inquired of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Do not go up, turn around behind them, and you shall come upon them in front of the mulberry trees.</dq>
[24] <dq>“And it shall be, when you hear <dn>את</dn> the sound of stepping in the tops of the mulberry trees, then act promptly, for then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall go out before you to strike the camp of the Philistines.”</dq>
[25] And Daviḏ did so, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded him, and smote <dn>את</dn> the Philistines from Geḇa as far as Gezer.

readings.title: The Breakthrough at Baal Peratsim
readings.text:
[1 Chronicles 14:8] And when the Philistines heard that Daviḏ had been anointed sovereign over all Yisra’ěl, all the Philistines went up to seek <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ. And Daviḏ heard and went out against them.
[9] And the Philistines came and made a raid on the Valley of Repha’im.
[10] And Daviḏ inquired of <dn>Elohim</dn>, saying, “Do I go up against the Philistines? And shall You give them into my hand?” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“Go up, and I shall give them into your hand.”</dq>
[11] And they went up to Ba‛al Peratsim, and Daviḏ struck them there. Then Daviḏ said, “<dn>Elohim</dn> has broken through <dn>את</dn> my enemies by my hand like a breakthrough of water.” So they called the name of that place Ba‛al Peratsim.
[12] And they left <dn>את</dn> their mighty ones there, so Daviḏ commanded, and they were burned with fire.
[13] And the Philistines once again made a raid on the valley.
[14] And Daviḏ again inquired of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>Elohim</dn> said to him, <dq>“Do not go up after them. Go around them, and come upon them in front of the mulberry trees.</dq>
[15] <dq>“And it shall be, when you hear <dn>את</dn> a sound of stepping in the tops of the mulberry trees, then go out to battle, for <dn>Elohim</dn> shall go out before you to strike <dn>את</dn> the camp of the Philistines.”</dq>
[16] And Daviḏ did as <dn>Elohim</dn> commanded him, and they struck <dn>את</dn> the army of the Philistines from Giḇ‛on as far as Gezer.
[17] And the name of Daviḏ went out into all lands, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> put <dn>את</dn> the dread of him upon all nations.

readings.title: The Capture of Zion
readings.text:
[2 Samuel 5:6] And the sovereign and his men went to Yerushalayim against the Yeḇusites, the inhabitants of the land. And they spoke to Daviḏ, saying, “Except you take away the blind and the lame, you are not going to come in here,” thinking, “Daviḏ is not going to come in here.”
[7] But Daviḏ captured <dn>את</dn> the stronghold of Tsiyon, the City of Daviḏ.
[8] And Daviḏ said on that day, “Anyone who strikes the Yeḇusites, let him go by the water-shaft and take the lame and the blind, who are hated by Daviḏ’s being.” That is why they say, “The blind and the lame do not come into the house.”
[9] And Daviḏ dwelt in the stronghold, and called it the City of Daviḏ. And Daviḏ built all around from the Millo and inward.
[10] And Daviḏ went on and became great, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts was with him.

readings.title: Jerusalem Becomes the City of David
readings.text:
[1 Chronicles 11:4] And Daviḏ and all Yisra’ěl went to Yerushalayim, which is Yeḇus, where the Yeḇusites were, the inhabitants of the land.
[5] And the inhabitants of Yeḇus said to Daviḏ, “You do not come in here.” But Daviḏ captured <dn>את</dn> the stronghold of Tsiyon, the City of Daviḏ.
[6] And Daviḏ said, “Whoever strikes the Yeḇusites first becomes chief and commander.” And Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah went up first, and became chief.
[7] And Daviḏ dwelt in the stronghold, so they called it the City of Daviḏ.
[8] And he built <dn>את</dn> the city around it, from Millo round about, and Yo’aḇ revived <dn>את</dn> the rest of the city.
[9] And Daviḏ went on and became great, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts was with him.

readings.title: The Length of David's Reign
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 3:4b] And he reigned there seven years and six new moons, and in Yerushalayim he reigned thirty-three years.

readings.title: David's House and Family
readings.text:
[2 Samuel 5:13] And Daviḏ took more concubines and wives from Yerushalayim, after he had come from Ḥeḇron, and more sons and daughters were born to Daviḏ.
[4] Daviḏ was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.
[5] In Ḥeḇron he reigned over Yehuḏah seven years and six new moons, and in Yerushalayim he reigned thirty-three years over all Yisra’ěl and Yehuḏah.
[11] Now Ḥiram sovereign of Tsor sent messengers to Daviḏ, and cedar trees, and carpenters and masons. And they built a house for Daviḏ.
[12] And Daviḏ knew that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had established him as sovereign over Yisra’ěl, and that <dn>He</dn> had exalted <dn>His</dn> reign, because of <dn>His</dn> people Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: Hiram Sends Builders
readings.text:
[1 Chronicles 14:1] And Ḥiram sovereign of Tsor sent messengers to Daviḏ, and cedar trees, with stonemasons and carpenters, to build him a house.
[2] And Daviḏ knew that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had established him as sovereign over Yisra’ěl, for his reign was highly exalted for the sake of <dn>His</dn> people Yisra’ěl.

readings.subsection: The First Attempt to Move the Ark
readings.title: David Consults the Assembly
readings.text:
[1 Chronicles 13:1] And Daviḏ consulted with the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and with every leader.
[2] And Daviḏ said to all the assembly of Yisra’ěl, “If it seems good to you, and if it is of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, let us send out to our brothers everywhere who are left in all the land of Yisra’ěl, and with them to the priests and Lěvites who are in their cities of their open lands, and let them be gathered to us;
[3] and let us bring the ark of our <dn>Elohim</dn> back to us, for we sought <dn>Him</dn> not since the days of Sha’ul.”
[4] And all the assembly agreed to do so, for the matter was right in the eyes of all the people.
[5] So Daviḏ assembled <dn>את</dn> all Yisra’ěl, from Shiḥor in Mitsrayim to as far as the entrance of Ḥamath, to bring <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> from Qiryath Ye‛arim.

readings.subsection: The First Attempt to Move the Ark
readings.title: The Ark on a New Cart
readings.text:
[2 Samuel 6:1] Now Daviḏ again gathered <dn>את</dn> all the chosen men of Yisra’ěl, thirty thousand.
[2] And Daviḏ rose up and went with all the people who were with him from Ba‛alě Yehuḏah, to bring up from there <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn>, that is called by the Name, the Name <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of Hosts, who dwells between the keruḇim.
[3] And they placed <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> on a new wagon, and brought it from the house of Aḇinaḏaḇ, which was on the hill. And Uzzah and Aḥyo, sons of Aḇinaḏaḇ, were leading the new wagon.
[4] And they brought it from the house of Aḇinaḏaḇ, which was on the hill, with the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn>. And Aḥyo was walking before the ark.
[5] And Daviḏ and all the house of Yisra’ěl were dancing before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, with all instruments of fir wood, and with lyres, and with harps, and with tambourines, and with sistrums, and with cymbals.
[6] And when they came to the threshing-floor of Naḵon, Uzzah reached out toward the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> and took hold of it, for the oxen stumbled.
[7] And the wrath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against Uzzah, and <dn>Elohim</dn> struck him there for the fault. And he died there by the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn$.
[8] And Daviḏ was displeased because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had broken out against Uzzah. And he called the name of the place Perets Uzzah, until this day.
[9] And Daviḏ was afraid of <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on that day, and said, “How shall the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> come to me?”
[10] And Daviḏ would not move <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with him into the City of Daviḏ, but Daviḏ turned it aside to the house of Oḇěḏ-Eḏom the Gittite.
[11] And the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> remained in the house of Oḇěḏ-Eḏom the Gittite three new moons, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> blessed <dn>את</dn> Oḇěḏ-Eḏom and <dn>את</dn> all his house.

readings.subsection: The First Attempt to Move the Ark
readings.title: The Death of Uzza
readings.text:
[1 Chronicles 13:6] And Daviḏ and all Yisra’ěl went up to Ba‛alah, to Qiryath Ye‛arim of Yehuḏah, to bring up from there the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who dwells between the keruḇim, where the Name is called on.
[7] And they placed <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> on a new wagon from the house of Aḇinaḏaḇ, and Uzza and Aḥyo were leading the wagon.
[8] And Daviḏ and all Yisra’ěl were playing before <dn>Elohim</dn> with all their might, and with songs, and with lyres, and with harps, and with tambourines, and with cymbals, and with trumpets.
[9] And when they came to the threshing-floor of Kiḏon, Uzza put out <dn>את</dn> his hand to hold <dn>את</dn> the ark, for the oxen stumbled.
[10] Then the wrath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against Uzza, and <dn>He</dn> struck him because he put his hand to the ark. And he died there before <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[11] And Daviḏ was displeased because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had broken out against Uzza, therefore that place is called Perets Uzza, until this day.
[12] And Daviḏ was afraid of <dn>את</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> that day, saying, “How shall I bring the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> to me?”
[13] So Daviḏ did not take <dn>את</dn> the ark with him into the City of Daviḏ, but took it aside into the house of Oḇěḏ-Eḏom the Gittite.
[14] And the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> remained with the household of Oḇěḏ-Eḏom in his house three new moons. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> blessed <dn>את</dn> the house of Oḇěḏ-Eḏom and <dn>את</dn> all that he had.
